chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.notes: Business/API data is covered by separate Business Terms + DPA (openai.com/policies hub lists them) but no single canonical DPA URL surfaced in search; not fabricating one.

claude.name: Claude
claude.notes: Consumer terms confirmed via direct fetch. Commercial Terms/DPA differ from consumer; used the consumer-facing set since ChatGPT-equivalent product here is the consumer app. privacy_policy originally pointed at the privacy.claude.com portal root, which is a nav/index page with no real prose (639 chars of menu text, confirmed empty extraction even after the HTML-cleaning fix) -- swapped to the direct 'Is my data used for model training?' article, which answers the exact fact the pipeline extracts.

gemini.name: Gemini
gemini.notes: Gemini Apps Privacy Notice supplements the general Google Privacy Policy rather than standing alone; used the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub as the most specific public page.

microsoft-copilot.name: Microsoft Copilot
microsoft-copilot.notes: Consumer Copilot (for individuals) product line, distinct from Microsoft 365 Copilot enterprise product which has its own terms.

github-copilot.name: GitHub Copilot
github-copilot.notes: Free/Pro/Pro+ vs Business/Enterprise have different data-use terms (Business/Enterprise excluded from AI-training data use per GitHub's own changelog) — worth surfacing to admin reviewer since one product covers two different data postures.

windsurf.name: Windsurf
windsurf.notes: Rebranded from Codeium; search only turned up a combined terms-of-service page (privacy content embedded in it), no standalone privacy-policy URL — not fabricating one. CORRECTION (2026-08-17): earlier note said 'acquired by OpenAI' — wrong. Confirmed live: windsurf.com/terms-of-service-individual now 308-redirects permanently to devin.ai/windsurf/terms-of-service-individual, i.e. Windsurf was acquired by Cognition (maker of Devin), not OpenAI. See DECISIONS_NEEDED.md for why this domain still can't be fetched.

sourcegraph-cody.name: Sourcegraph Cody
sourcegraph-cody.notes: Confirmed still active as of June 2026 privacy policy update; Cody is now bundled under Sourcegraph's broader "AI Tools" umbrella rather than a standalone product name.

adobe-firefly.name: Adobe Firefly
adobe-firefly.notes: No Firefly-specific privacy policy URL exists separately — Firefly is covered by Adobe's general Privacy Policy plus a dedicated 'data and content usage' explainer page, used here as the closest thing to a security/trust page.

grammarly.name: Grammarly
grammarly.notes: Individual-account privacy policy explicitly does not cover Business/Education/Pro-under-org accounts, which fall under a separate DPA — same two-tier pattern as GitHub Copilot.

jasper.name: Jasper
jasper.notes: DPA exists but must be separately executed by customers per Jasper's own terms; no public standalone DPA URL found.

notion-ai.name: Notion AI
notion-ai.notes: Used the AI-specific security/privacy practices page as the closest thing to AI-scoped terms; general Notion ToS covers the rest of the product.

zoom-ai-companion.name: Zoom AI Companion
zoom-ai-companion.notes: Zoom's general Terms of Service page used since no AI Companion-specific ToS URL surfaced separately from the privacy/security explainer.

tabnine.name: Tabnine
tabnine.notes: Privacy policy is thin on whether code is used for training -- the concrete 'zero data retention' claim lives on a separate marketing page (tabnine.com/code-privacy) that isn't a legal document, so not substituted in as the source of record. Trust center is SafeBase-hosted (third-party), same pattern as other vendor trust portals in this batch -- confirmed genuine, not a spoof.

amazon-q-developer.name: Amazon Q Developer
amazon-q-developer.notes: SHARED APEX DOMAIN (aws.amazon.com covers all AWS services) -- flag for shared_domain like Gemini/Microsoft Copilot in the first batch; the general AWS Privacy Notice and Service Terms are not Q-Developer-specific. Used the AWS docs data-protection page as security_trust_page since it's the most product-scoped source and links onward to the real opt-out mechanism (docs.aws.amazon.com/.../opt-out-IDE.html) and the service-improvement page explaining how content may be used. Confirmed via direct fetch (not a search summary) -- got real AWS doc markdown, not a nav shell.

jetbrains-ai-assistant.name: JetBrains AI Assistant
jetbrains-ai-assistant.notes: AI-specific ToS states inputs/outputs will NOT be used to train language models without express permission -- a clearer no-default-training stance than most tools in this batch. DPA page is dated Version 1.3 / April 27, 2022 -- old relative to the 2025-dated AI ToS it's linked from; flagging staleness, not swapping it for a guess.

bolt-new.name: Bolt.new
bolt-new.notes: Bolt.new has no standalone legal docs -- StackBlitz (the parent company/IDE product) is the entity and its Privacy Policy/ToS explicitly cover Bolt. Confirmed the privacy policy addresses AI-input training use directly (tiered opt-out by plan). A separate merch-shop ToS at shop.bolt.new/pages/terms-of-service exists but is irrelevant (covers t-shirt purchases, not the product) -- not used.

v0.name: v0
v0.notes: SHARED APEX DOMAIN for the privacy/terms/DPA docs (vercel.com covers Vercel's whole hosting platform, not just v0) -- same flag as Amazon Q Developer. Used v0.app/policy (confirmed genuine, product-specific) as the security_trust_page slot since it's the one v0-scoped legal doc and covers the actual fact this pipeline extracts: tiered model-training opt-in/opt-out by plan tier.

ideogram.name: Ideogram
ideogram.notes: Privacy policy confirms user data is used to 'train the models that power our Services' with no opt-out mechanism found, and no GDPR-specific section (policy leans CCPA/state-law framing). Worth a clear-eyed read before publishing as compliant on anything.

luma-ai.name: Luma AI (Dream Machine)
luma-ai.notes: Confirms data used to 'train, develop, and improve' its AI/ML models; no explicit training opt-out found (only marketing-email opt-out), despite an otherwise thorough GDPR rights section. Enterprise customers are carved out as controllers under their own terms.

suno.name: Suno
suno.notes: ToS grants Suno a broad perpetual license over submissions/outputs 'in connection with...improvement of our products and services, including...artificial intelligence and machine learning models' -- confirmed via direct fetch. Free vs. paid tiers have different output-ownership terms, similar two-tier pattern to GitHub Copilot/Grammarly in the first batch.

heygen.name: HeyGen
heygen.notes: One of the few tools in this batch with an explicit AI-training opt-out reachable by contacting privacy@heygen.com (Section 4 of the privacy policy) rather than just a settings toggle. security.heygen.com is a Drata-hosted trust portal (third-party-hosted, same pattern as Tabnine's SafeBase portal) -- confirmed genuine, not mistaken for an unrelated org's trust center.

synthesia.name: Synthesia
synthesia.notes: Used the consumer-facing User Terms of Service (not Customer Terms of Service, which is the B2B contract) to match this batch's individual-checker ICP, same distinction made for ChatGPT/GitHub Copilot in the first batch. Privacy policy does not clearly state whether personal data (as opposed to video/avatar content generally) is used for model training -- flagging the gap rather than guessing.

wordtune.name: Wordtune
wordtune.notes: Privacy policy says content is used to 'improve, enhance and develop the Services' but doesn't clearly say whether that includes AI model training specifically -- ambiguous rather than silent. Confirmed strong GDPR section otherwise.

sudowrite.name: Sudowrite
sudowrite.notes: FLAG FOR REVIEWER: privacy policy is dated October 6, 2020 and never mentions AI, model training, or generative features at all, despite Sudowrite being an AI fiction-writing tool today -- reads as a stale template the company hasn't updated to cover its actual product. Confirmed genuine (not fabricated), just outdated; extraction will likely come back with null training-related facts, which is an honest reflection of the source, not a pipeline bug.

you-com.name: You.com
you-com.notes: Privacy policy explicitly states uploaded/prompt data 'will not be used for developing, improving, or training third party AI and/or ML models' -- one of the clearer no-third-party-training statements in this batch (says nothing about You.com's own first-party models, worth noting).

kagi.name: Kagi
kagi.notes: No separate terms-of-service URL surfaced distinct from the privacy policy -- Kagi's site structures both under /privacy plus a linked 'Privacy Rights Addendum' for GDPR/CCPA specifics; used the same URL for both fields rather than fabricate a separate ToS link. Policy states Kagi does not use personal data or prompts to train AI models and does not sell data -- a genuinely privacy-first stance consistent with its no-ads subscription business model.

fireflies-ai.name: Fireflies.ai
fireflies-ai.notes: Explicit statement that meeting content/personal data is not used to train AI models and vendors are contractually barred from training on it -- one of the strongest no-training claims found in this batch.

rev.name: Rev
rev.notes: Policy doesn't explicitly address AI-model-training use of transcripts/audio, a notable gap for a company whose product is AI-assisted transcription -- flagging rather than inferring an answer from marketing copy that says 'never uses customer content to train external AI models' (that claim wasn't confirmed inside the legal document itself).

speechify.name: Speechify
speechify.notes: Speechify also runs separate Studio-specific privacy/terms pages (speechify.com/studio-privacy, speechify.com/studio-terms) for its voice-cloning/dubbing product line -- used the main consumer text-to-speech app's policy since that's the product a casual checker would have installed, not the Studio B2B tool.

character-ai.name: Character.AI
character-ai.notes: FLAG FOR REVIEWER: both URLs are confirmed genuine and resolve on the real character.ai domain (via 308 redirects from policies.character.ai, which is the canonical link Character.AI itself publishes) -- but the site is a client-rendered SPA, so WebFetch only received the page shell/tagline, not policy prose, on every attempt. This is the same failure mode as Claude's original nav-page issue in the first batch, except here it's a rendering limitation, not a wrong URL -- the backend's own fetcher may hit the same wall depending on whether it executes JS. Also checked and explicitly rejected a lookalike domain, characterai.cc, which appeared in search results claiming to host Character.AI's terms -- it is not Character.AI's domain and was not used anywhere in this record.

poe.name: Poe
poe.notes: Poe's privacy policy is a supplement to the main Quora Privacy Policy (incorporated by reference) rather than fully standalone -- confirmed it explicitly discloses that third-party AI model providers and bot creators can receive full chat contents/uploaded files. No clear opt-out mechanism for that sharing found within the Poe-specific document itself.

granola.name: Granola
granola.notes: Confirms Granola does not allow OpenAI/Anthropic/other third-party model providers to train on customer data, only uses de-identified/aggregated data for its own model improvement, and that's opt-outable in account settings (opt-out is default-off for Enterprise). Newer, smaller consumer-facing tool -- exactly the category the founder asked this batch to cover.

deepl.name: DeepL
deepl.notes: Clean two-tier compliance story confirmed directly in both the privacy policy and this free-service ToS: free-tier submissions ARE used to train/improve DeepL's models (temporary retention), Pro/paid submissions explicitly are NOT. This is a genuinely different compliance answer depending on which tier a user is on -- worth surfacing to the reviewer the same way the free-vs-paid GitHub Copilot split was flagged in the first batch. Used the free-service Terms of Use (matches this batch's individual/casual ICP) rather than the Pro/Enterprise license variants, which are separate documents.
